title: Choose Scaur's visual world
question: A fresh, contemporary hand. The roll assigned Heat Map. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Heat Map
options.lineage: thermal-camera imaging, as used in 2020s insulation and apparel testing
options.thesis: Scaur shows what a layer does, not just what it looks like: flip any product or kit into a thermal view and watch it hold heat.
materials: clean modern grotesk on a cool light ground
options.viewport: A light, photo-led hero: a hard-cropped runner in the shell on the left, a 'Photo / Thermal' switch that turns the image into a thermal render as the headline explains the layering system, and one 'Build your kit' action.
options.risk: Glowing gradients can tip into the dark-neon look every AI store ships; the thermal scale only appears where it encodes warmth, and the store itself stays light and photo-led. Thermal views are stylised illustrations and labelled as such.

raised.raise: Depth comes only from layers overlapping in flat colour: no drop shadows, no blur, no glass.
One temperature axis runs through the whole store; every product and kit sits on it, so warmth ratings compare at a glance.
The kit builder is four fixed slots (base, mid, insulation, shell) that never wrap; an empty kit is four quiet slots inviting a pick.
Adding a layer visibly pushes warmth outward from the body in the thermal view, so every choice shows its effect.
Choosing a colourway floods the product stage with that colour, a decisive cut rather than a fade.

options.label: Layer Stack
options.lineage: 2020s flagship product pages: scroll-driven exploded views
options.thesis: The layering system as one exploded stack: base, mid, insulation and shell float apart as you scroll, each labelled with what it does.
options.viewport: Four translucent garment layers stacked in 3D, pulling apart on scroll with a rating beside each, and 'Build your kit' pinned below.
options.risk: The Apple-style scroll-exploded view is where most premium product pages land in 2026, so it is familiar; it also needs clean product cut-outs and a heavier 3D budget.

options.label: Box Wall
options.thesis: Browse the collection like a wall of shoe boxes: every end label reads name, colourway and a size run you can see is in stock.
options.viewport: A wall of product boxes, one sliding half out with its lid lifting to show the garment and its live size run.
options.case: Very clear for variants and stock (colourway and size run on every label), and contemporary retail culture; loses on audience, because it speaks sneakerheads more than mountain buyers.
options.risk: Can feel like a sneaker shop wearing an outdoor brand's products.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.thesis: Figures built from separately cut layers of flat colour.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel built up layer by layer.
options.case: Layering reads literally, but folk craft is not the 2026 look you asked for.
options.risk: Reads as folk art, not technical apparel.
options.kept: Depth by overlap only: no shadows, blur or glass.

options.label: Horizon Grid
options.thesis: Everything sits on one receding horizon.
options.viewport: A wireframe grid running to a striped sun.
options.case: Pure retro, the opposite of what you asked for.
options.kept: One shared axis: a single temperature scale every product sits on.

options.label: Step Sequencer
options.thesis: Sixteen lit keys under a running chase light.
options.viewport: A step row you punch a pattern into.
options.case: Retro hardware; hikers do not identify with it.
options.kept: Fixed slots that never wrap: the kit builder's four layer slots.

options.label: Floated Pigment
options.thesis: Every mark made by moving liquid colour.
options.viewport: A marbled bath you comb into shape.
options.case: Beautiful, but says nothing about clothing or conditions.
options.kept: Each action visibly displaces the last: warmth spreads outward as layers are added.

options.label: Title Card
options.thesis: Flat colour fields sliced by hard bars, titles colliding.
options.viewport: A frozen silhouette against a flooded colour field.
options.case: Stylish but retro, and fights product clarity.
options.kept: A chosen colourway floods the product stage in one hard cut.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The outdoor-brand store everyone knows: big mountain photography, white product grid, one bold accent.
canonCard.viewport: A full-width ridge photo with a headline and 'Shop now', then a four-up product grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the stores it would compete with, by design.
